request.user:
Change c0226. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. III; 1831 Ch. XI.

Context before (unchanged): "As soon as morning dawned, I crept from my kennel, that I might view the adjacent cottage, and discover if I could remain in the habitation I had found.

1818 text: It was situated against the back of the cottage, and surrounded on the sides which were exposed by a pig-stye and a clear pool of water. One part was open, and by that I had crept in; but now I covered every crevice by which I might be perceived with stones and wood, yet in such a manner that I might move them on occasion to pass out: all the light I enjoyed came through the stye, and that was sufficient for me.

1831 text: It was situated against the back of the cottage, and surrounded on the sides which were exposed by a pig-sty and a clear pool of water. One part was open, and by that I had crept in; but now I covered every crevice by which I might be perceived with stones and wood, yet in such a manner that I might move them on occasion to pass out: all the light I enjoyed came through the sty, and that was sufficient for me.

Diff: It was situated against the back of the cottage, and surrounded on the sides which were exposed by a [-pig-stye-] {+pig-sty+} and a clear pool of water. One part was open, and by that I had crept in; but now I covered every crevice by which I might be perceived with stones and wood, yet in such a manner that I might move them on occasion to pass out: all the light I enjoyed came through the [-stye-] {+sty+} , and that was sufficient for me.

Context after (unchanged): "Having thus arranged my dwelling, and carpeted it with clean straw, I retired; for I saw the figure of a man at a distance, and I remembered too well my treatment the night before, to trust myself in his power.

result.rationale: Only orthography changes: 'stye' becomes 'sty' (pig-stye to pig-sty, stye to sty). The wording, meaning, and description of the creature's hovel are unchanged.
